brief: JPM's afternoon update ties today's AI/semis selloff to a specific chain: Broadcom CEO Hock Tan warned financing could become a bigger bottleneck than chip supply, a weekend sell-side note reignited powered-shell shortage fears (up to 19GW next year, more in 2028), and CXMT's "4F2" DRAM news added to memory weakness, all compounding into a holiday-thin session ahead of Wednesday's expected private frontier-lab investor meeting. That drove SOXX -2.6% and DRAM -4.3% even though SPX breadth stayed over 60% positive, with capital rotating into Mag 7/Internet. Separately, JPM's factor analyst argues semiconductor sentiment has reverted to May levels and now sits above the 99th percentile, the kind of vertical Quality-factor jump last seen in the 2023 regional-bank crisis and the October 2023 rate backup, both of which reversed only after Fed intervention, so he flags reversal risk around the CPI release and this month's Fed meeting if the Fed turns dovish. Oil extended its rally as a Houthi attack on Riyadh's airport and Russian strikes on Ukrainian energy sites despite the announced ceasefire weakened the Trump-Russia diesel de-escalation story. Meta launched Muse Wonder (formerly Watermelon) today. JPM reiterates its Tactically Bullish view into earnings, citing the SOX's pullback as an inflection point backed by Hynix/Samsung earnings strength.
